findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.evidence: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.

extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.evidence: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797.

extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

correlate.executive_summary: The assessment found several HTTP security hardening issues on https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/, primarily missing security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy). No product/version CVE matches were available for the detected platform, so no severity or confidence was upgraded based on CVE data. Additional informational findings include platform fingerprinting evidence for Heroku and uncommon reporting headers (NEL / report-to / reporting-endpoints) which also exposed a timestamp-like value. Overall these are configuration/hardening issues; no confirmed high-risk product-specific vulnerabilities were identified by the provided scans.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header
findings.evidence: va (zap) reported 'Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set' on https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml; recon also noted CSP not set. ZAP output explains CSP is missing and its role in mitigating XSS/data injection.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header not set
findings.evidence: recon reported 'Missing security header: strict-transport-security' for https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/; va (zap) reported 'Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set' on the root and on /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml.

findings.title: Missing X-Frame-Options header (anti-clickjacking)
findings.evidence: recon reported 'Missing security header: x-frame-options' for https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/ (confirmed). va (nikto) also reported 'The anti-clickjacking X-Frame-Options header is not present.' on https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com:443/.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options header
findings.evidence: recon reported 'Missing security header: x-content-type-options' for https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/ (response did not set X-Content-Type-Options).

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy header
findings.evidence: recon reported 'Missing security header: referrer-policy' for https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com/ (response did not set Referrer-Policy).

findings.title: Uncommon reporting headers (NEL / report-to / reporting-endpoints) and potential timestamp disclosure
findings.evidence: va (nikto) observed uncommon headers: 'nel' with contents {"report_to":"heroku-nel",...}, 'reporting-endpoints' with a heroku-nel URL, and 'report-to' with a heroku-nel value on https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com:443/. va (zap) reported 'Timestamp Disclosure - Unix' for Reporting-Endpoints parameter(s) (suspected). These indicate browser network error logging/reporting headers are present and that a timestamp-like value was disclosed; further manual review is suggested.

findings.title: Platform fingerprint: Heroku (server/via headers)
findings.evidence: recon detected 'Heroku' via Server header hints (Header 'Server': 'Heroku'). va (nikto) retrieved header '1.1 heroku-router' in response headers, supporting the Heroku platform fingerprint.

correlate.deduplication_notes: Findings reporting missing HTTP security headers from multiple agents were merged: recon and va/ZAP Nikto entries referencing CSP, HSTS and X-Frame-Options were consolidated into single findings per header. Multiple instances of CSP and HSTS reported on root, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml were combined into single findings covering those endpoints. Nikto's multiple 'NEL/report-to/reporting-endpoints' entries were grouped together and correlated with ZAP's timestamp-disclosure note into one low-confidence finding about reporting headers and a possible timestamp leak. The Heroku platform fingerprint and nikto '1.1 heroku-router' header were combined into a single tech_fingerprint finding. No CVEs were applied because no product/version data was available to match against NVD entries.
